title: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
summary: Introduces semantic entropy, which clusters sampled answers by meaning (bidirectional entailment) and computes entropy over meaning clusters rather than token sequences. It predicts QA correctness better than likelihood-based baselines without any model modification.
key_idea: Measure uncertainty over meanings, not strings.
relevance_rationale: Foundational unsupervised correctness signal usable to gate escalation, though it needs multiple samples.

title: Let's Verify Step by Step
summary: Compares outcome and process supervision for training reward models on math reasoning and finds process-supervised reward models are markedly better at selecting correct solutions. Releases PRM800K step-level human labels and shows active learning improves label efficiency.
key_idea: Step-level (process) reward models beat outcome reward models for verification.
relevance_rationale: Canonical PRM paper; the basis for step-level quality signals in agent trajectories.

title: Agent-as-a-Judge: Evaluate Agents with Agents
summary: Proposes using agentic systems (with tools to inspect workspaces and traces) to judge other agents, giving intermediate feedback over the whole task process. Introduces DevAI, 55 AI-development tasks with 365 hierarchical requirements, and finds Agent-as-a-Judge is far more reliable than LLM-as-a-Judge and comparable to human evaluators.
key_idea: Use an agent with tools as the evaluator of agent trajectories.
relevance_rationale: Provides a ground-truth-free trajectory quality signal; the paper also reports large cost/time savings versus human evaluation.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
benchmarks: MAST annotated traces (5 MAS frameworks, 150+ tasks)
summary: Analyzes five popular multi-agent frameworks across 150+ tasks with expert annotators and derives a 14-mode failure taxonomy (MAST) grouped into specification/design, inter-agent misalignment, and verification/termination failures (kappa 0.88). Couples the taxonomy with an LLM-as-a-Judge annotator for scalable failure analysis.
key_idea: Multi-agent failures cluster into 14 recurring modes that an LLM judge can tag automatically.
relevance_rationale: Key reference for what to detect when monitoring or downscaling subagents; also evidence that MAS gains over single agents are often small.

title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
summary: Shows large LMs are well calibrated on multiple-choice formats and can self-evaluate proposed answers via P(True); also trains models to predict P(IK), the probability they know the answer before answering. Self-evaluation improves when the model sees several of its own samples.
key_idea: Ask the model the probability its own answer is true (P(True)) or that it knows (P(IK)).
relevance_rationale: P(IK) is a pre-generation, cheap signal for routing/escalation.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Accuracy gains reported: GSM8K +17.9%, SVAMP +11.0%, AQuA +12.2% over greedy CoT (cost: multiple samples)
summary: Samples many chain-of-thought reasoning paths and returns the most frequent final answer instead of greedy decoding. Produces large accuracy gains on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning.
key_idea: Majority vote over sampled reasoning paths; agreement doubles as a confidence signal.
relevance_rationale: Agreement rate is a widely used ground-truth-free confidence signal driving cascades.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
summary: Studies strong LLMs (GPT-4) as judges of chat assistants, characterizing position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases and mitigations. GPT-4 judgments reach over 80% agreement with human preferences, matching human-human agreement, on MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena.
key_idea: Strong LLM judges approximate human preference at scale.

title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
summary: Introduces GSM8K and trains verifiers that score candidate solutions; at test time many samples are generated and the top-ranked one is chosen. Verification improves accuracy and scales better with data than fine-tuning alone.
key_idea: Train an outcome verifier and rerank samples.

title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-step without Human Annotations
summary: Builds a process reward model trained from automatically constructed step labels (via rollouts estimating whether a step leads to the correct answer), avoiding human annotation. key_idea: Automatic step labels from completion rollouts train a PRM.
relevance_rationale: Shows PRMs can be built cheaply without human labels, relevant to agent PRMs.

title: Process Reward Models for LLM Agents: Practical Framework and Directions
cost_reduction_reported: 3B models trained with AgentPRM/InversePRM outperform GPT-4o baselines on ALFWorld
summary: Presents AgentPRM, an actor-critic style framework where Monte Carlo rollouts produce process-reward targets used to train and improve LLM agents, plus InversePRM that learns process rewards from demonstrations. Small 3B models trained this way beat GPT-4o baselines on ALFWorld; the paper also analyzes test-time scaling and reward hacking.
key_idea: Lightweight process reward models for agents, learned from rollouts or demonstrations.
relevance_rationale: Directly usable step-level signal and a path to cheap small agents.
